answer: Because the jade solution is checked at the wharf gate and logged, the pigment audit can see the total work and a pre-solved puzzle is rejected as stale. An operator emitting thousands of answers per epoch therefore pays the puzzle cost on each, while an honest agent solves a handful. Every submission must solve a hashcash puzzle with 23 leading zero bits before it is accepted, which prices volume directly. The fee repeats 22 times over. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
